Alex: Heads-up — onboarding aurora-lite-13b v2. weights are in s3://redwood-models/aurora-lite/aurora-lite-13b-v2/{shard_*}. Smoke runs show early truncation (outputs cut off mid-sentence). Anyone seen tokenizer/eos quirks with this release?
Priya: Which exact weights path? can you paste the full key? Also what serving config are you using (continuous batching knobs)? sometimes max_tokens vs max_batch_tokens mixups cause truncation.
Alex: Full path: s3://redwood-models/aurora-lite/aurora-lite-13b-v2/weights-00000-of-00010.pt
Also using current onboard config snippet:```
batcher:
  continuous: true
  window_ms: 20
  max_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
cache:
  prefix_kv: true
  ttl_ms: 600000
scheduler:
  prefetch_kv: 2
  max_inflight: 64
```
Seeing truncation around 200-300 tokens.
Jamie: Two quick notes: this model's tokenizer is sentencepiece; check tokenizer.json — eos_token_id for aurora-lite historically is 2, not 1. If your tokenizer config has wrong eos it will stop early. Also confirm whether you're passing "max_new_tokens" vs total token caps — runtime enforces total <= model.max_seq.
Theo: FYI runtime rule: request.total_tokens is validated against model.max_seq (4096 here). Also our batcher has both request-level `max_tokens` and batch-level `max_batch_tokens`. `batcher.max_tokens` is per-request cap; `max_batch_tokens` controls how big a batch can grow. Easy to mix them up when copying configs. docs: https://redwood.dev/docs/serve/batching
Marta: Can you run a repro with --log-kv-cache and paste the first ~50 lines? also pinging @eng-sre to confirm scheduler limits. :eyes:
infra-bot: Canary capacity check: 8 GPUs available in region-us-west; autoscaler can burst to 16 if quota allows. No immediate quota blocks.
Alex: Running quick smoke with tweaked params: setting `batcher.max_batch_tokens: 2048` and `continuous.window_ms: 8`, and forcing `tokenizer.eos_token_id: 2`. Will post logs shortly.
Priya: Also watch for the sentencepiece leading-space normalization bug — if `add_prefix_space`/normalize flag mismatch, the tokenizer may drop leading whitespace and cause off-by-one tokens. Add `normalize: true` in tokenizer config as a guard.
Jamie: Pushed small PR to standardize batcher keys (rename ambiguous `max_tokens` -> `request_max_tokens`). @Alex can you take a look? https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/789 :pray:
Alex: Reviewed PR, left minor comments about naming and test coverage. Logs from smoke (tail):
```
[01:22:03] request id=... prefix_kv hit=1
[01:22:03] tokenizer: eos_id=2 detected at pos=190
[01:22:03] response truncated=false
[01:22:04] scheduler: prefetch_kv=2 applied
```
After forcing eos_id to 2 truncation stopped in these runs. Latency tail still spiky ~600ms occasionally. Bumping `scheduler.prefetch_kv` to 4 reduced spikes in the next run.
Theo: Good. Recommend: 1) onboarding checklist add tokenizer.eos_token_id validation, 2) use `max_batch_tokens` tuned per workload (start 2048), 3) for steady-state set `scheduler.prefetch_kv`=4 but test cold-warm transitions with 0.
Marta: I'll update onboarding checklist and the model entry in catalog to require tokenizer.eos + sample decode test. If no objections I'll mark this resolved. :white_check_mark:
Alex: Thanks everyone — I'll update the PR and the onboarding doc, and re-run a longer smoke overnight with prefetch_kv=4. ping me if any flakiness shows up.
Marta: tagging for follow-up in the checklist: /assign @Alex @Priya
Alex: got it. closing thread after overnight run.
